records.scope: Classical probability-space/null-set background needed to state effective tests; computable measures; effective open sets; integral-test formulations.
records.why_it_matters: Test-based randomness definitions depend on exactly which null sets/measures/tests are effectively present.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S005 now has exact primary definitions for computable metric spaces, computable probability measures, computable probability spaces, effective-open/integral tests and arbitrary-measure uniform tests.

The inspected general-space framework is computable-metric-space based. Arbitrary represented-space probability formalisms were not separately primary-inspected, and classical measure theory beyond randomness-relevant machinery remains outside scope.
next_actions: Later close remaining foundational gaps only where they affect randomness definitions or theorem hypotheses; do not expand into a general computable-analysis survey.

records.area: Historical statistical randomness, normality, von Mises and Church selection
records.scope: Normal numbers/statistical frequency tests; collectives; admissible place selections; Church effectivization; later stochasticity terminology.
records.why_it_matters: Separates frequency/selection approaches from stronger effective-test and betting notions and prevents ahistorical equivalence claims.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Borel and von Mises original sources not yet catalogued directly; Church source statement inspected; later terminology crosswalk incomplete.
next_actions: Add primary Borel/von Mises records and source-supported relationships among normality, Church stochasticity and modern notions.

records.area: Martin-Löf randomness and effective null tests
records.scope: Core definitions, universal tests, equivalent formulations and foundational history for individual infinite sequences.
records.why_it_matters: Central benchmark notion against which many weaker, stronger, relative and generalized notions are calibrated.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Original 1966 paper abstract inspected but its internal theorem statements/proofs were not yet fully indexed.
next_actions: Inspect original statements and add Solovay-test, martingale and further complexity characterizations with primary sources.

records.area: Schnorr, computable, Kurtz and weak randomness notions
records.scope: Major weaker notions; exact test/betting resources; strictness and separation theorems; weak-n hierarchy where relevant.
records.why_it_matters: These notions expose how changes in effectivity/resource constraints alter randomness and provide a calibrated local landscape around Martin-Löf randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Schnorr's original 1971 book and unified article remain METADATA_ONLY internally; Kurtz's 1981 thesis remains METADATA_ONLY.

P1-S003 now has statement-level ordinary oracle formulations for computable, Schnorr and Kurtz randomness plus uniform-relative Schnorr/computable formulations, but generalized-measure versions are not normalized here.
Ordinary and uniformly relative Schnorr/computable randomness are deliberately not collapsed; van-Lambalgen behavior depends on this distinction.
next_actions: If accessible, close the original Schnorr/Kurtz internal-statement gap; otherwise preserve it.
Connect weaker notions to generalized computable measures/spaces in a later bounded session without importing fair-coin conventions by analogy.

records.area: Martingale, betting, prediction and selection-rule characterizations
records.scope: Monotone martingales, computable/lower-semicomputable betting, non-monotone Kolmogorov-Loveland strategies, selection rules and unpredictability paradigms.
records.why_it_matters: Provides the unpredictability axis and reveals where adaptive/non-monotonic access changes a randomness notion.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S002 now has primary statement-level computable-martingale, Schnorr bounded-rate martingale and Kurtz weak-martingale formulations, but several historical martingale sources and nonmonotone/KL machinery remain uninspected beyond existing records.
next_actions: Acquire remaining historical martingale characterization sources and deepen KL/nonmonotonic machinery; preserve exact success/rate conventions.

records.area: Kolmogorov complexity, algorithmic information and incompressibility
records.scope: Plain and prefix-free complexity; coding/incompressibility characterizations; finite-string and infinite-sequence interfaces.
records.why_it_matters: Complexity provides a second foundational characterization axis and is central to lowness, dimension and random-real theory.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Kolmogorov 1965 primary text only metadata-inspected.

P1-S007 adds statement-level self-delimiting H/K evidence connecting finite-string complexity to the quantified initial-segment characterization of infinite-sequence Martin-Löf randomness; no broader complexity-family survey was opened.
next_actions: Inspect primary complexity definitions and original incompressibility-characterization sources; add conditional/monotone variants only where randomness-relevant.

records.scope: Constructive/effective Hausdorff dimension, supergales, complexity-rate characterizations and finite-string dimension.
records.why_it_matters: Quantifies degrees of algorithmic information/randomness rather than only binary pass/fail notions.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: Exact supergale definition not statement-inspected, so no DEF record yet.
next_actions: Inspect primary definitions and distinguish constructive dimension, strong dimension and resource-bounded variants.

records.scope: Relativized tests/complexity/betting notions; oracle dependence; van Lambalgen-type phenomena; relative random reals.
records.why_it_matters: Relativization is structurally central to lowness, bases, jumps and higher notions.

Uniform-versus-ordinary relativization is explicit for Schnorr/computable randomness. Arbitrary measures/spaces and a primary inspection of the original Merkle et al. counterexamples were not pursued in this bounded session.

If needed for the global relation graph, inspect the original counterexample paper behind failure of naive van-Lambalgen directions for ordinary Schnorr/computable randomness; do not infer it from definitions.

records.area: Lowness notions and bases for randomness
records.scope: Low-for-randomness classes, K-triviality, bases for randomness, traceability interfaces and computational weakness.

next_actions: Expand lowness/bases only in a dedicated primary-source tranche; preserve the P1-S003 ordinary/uniform relativization distinction where relevant.

records.scope: 2-randomness, n-randomness, weak-2 comparisons, Demuth randomness and other stronger effective-test notions.

known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S004 now has statement-level primary definitions for Demuth, difference, balanced and Oberwolfach randomness, together with the existing weak-n and jump-based n-randomness records.

Demuth's 1982 original was recovered and inspected, but it is Russian and uses historical constructive notation restricted to arithmetical reals; the modern all-real normal form is cross-checked through SRC-0016/SRC-0035 rather than presented as a verbatim translation.
The source-specific distinction between Demuth's Solovay passing and the ordinary weak-Demuth passing used for balanced/Oberwolfach tests is now explicit.
Relations to arbitrary computable measures/spaces, broader weak/partial Demuth variants and higher-randomness analogues remain outside this bounded tranche.
next_actions: Retain this stratum as partial until broader stronger-test variants and any generalized-measure/higher cross-links needed for Gate 1 are inspected; do not infer missing arrows from the current definitions.
If historical priority details become decision-relevant, obtain an independent translation/secondary philological check for the 1982 Demuth notation rather than guessing from the scan.

records.scope: Δ1_1-, Π1_1-Martin-Löf-, Π1_1-randomness, higher weak-2/difference notions and lowness at higher levels.
records.why_it_matters: Tests which classical randomness structures persist under higher computability and where genuinely different phenomena arise.

records.scope: Preservation under effective measure-preserving maps; existence of random preimages; notion-specific failures and maximality principles.

The historical Shen antecedent for Martin-Löf no-randomness-from-nothing was not independently recovered as an original standalone source; the exact modern statements are preserved from inspected primary papers.
No global conservation/NRFN table beyond the exact notions needed for this session is promoted; fair-coin stronger-randomness records from P1-S004 remain scoped as before.
next_actions: Only if needed for Gate-1 completeness, trace the earliest standalone Martin-Löf NRFN provenance and any remaining exact map-class variants without reopening a broad stronger-randomness survey.

records.area: Computable probability spaces and randomness beyond Cantor space
records.scope: Computable metric/probability spaces, arbitrary computable measures, uniform tests, isomorphisms and non-binary domains.
records.why_it_matters: Prevents the programme from mistaking Cantor-space presentation choices for intrinsic features of randomness.
known_retrieval_access_limitations: P1-S005 now has statement-level primary definitions for computable metric/probability spaces, generalized Martin-Löf and Schnorr tests, measure-parameter uniform tests, morphisms/isomorphisms, binary representations, the atomless Lebesgue-space theorem, and exact conservation/invariance links.
The general Cantor representation uses an appropriate computable measure, not automatically fair coin. Atomlessness is required for the stronger fixed nonatomic/Lebesgue model.
Arbitrary represented-space formalisms beyond the inspected computable-metric-space setting remain uninspected; no theorem is inferred for them by analogy.
next_actions: A later coverage audit should decide whether the current primary computable-metric-space stratum is sufficient for Gate 1 or whether one bounded represented-space source is still needed.

records.scope: Typicality, effective ergodic theorems, mixing computable dynamics and probability-theoretic characterizations tied to individual randomness.

next_actions: Acquire primary effective Birkhoff/ergodic characterization literature.

records.area: Finite strings, random reals, left-c.e. reals and Ω
records.scope: Randomness/patternlessness for finite strings; infinite reals as binary sequences; left-c.e. random reals; Chaitin Ω and related representations.

(historical r.e.) reals, prefix-free halting probabilities, Chaitin Ω-numbers, and the exact random-left-c.e./Ω characterization.

The Solovay draft cited by the 2001 primary papers was not independently recovered at statement level in this bounded pass; no theorem detail is promoted from the inaccessible manuscript.
The 2001 primary sources use 'recursively enumerable real'; P1-S007 normalizes this to the modern alias 'left-c.e. real' while preserving the source vocabulary and one-sided approximation definition.
No arbitrary left-c.e. real is identified as random. Universality is kept explicit whenever Martin-Löf randomness of a halting probability is asserted.
No relative-Ω/oracle survey, generalized-measure transfer, stronger-test transfer or category analogy was opened.
next_actions: If later Phase-1 completeness requires historical provenance beyond the present statement-level core, inspect the 1966/1969 Chaitin internals and the Solovay draft if accessible; otherwise preserve their access gaps explicitly.
Keep future Ω additions hypothesis-exact: distinguish arbitrary prefix-free halting probabilities from universal-machine Ω-numbers and preserve binary-representation conventions.
